facts.fact: a Feistel-network permutation since the Mantis cooldown
replaced the affine/LCG permutation p(x) = (a * x + b) % N

citations.claim: To achieve reproducible shuffling at runtime, pseudo-random permutations over training data blocks are computed inside the data loader.
Marin previously used an affine/LCG permutation, choosing integers a and b with gcd(a, N) = 1 for dataset length N, and mapping indices by p(x) = (a * x + b) % N.

In Mantis, Marin switched to a Feistel-network permutation, a pseudo-random permutation over the index domain that splits the bit representation into halves and applies several mixing rounds with per-round keys.
Marin committed to using the Feistel shuffle going forward after it resolved earlier phase shift effects and improved validation losses.

answer.answer: Marin computes pseudo-random permutations over training data blocks inside the data loader. It previously used an affine/linear congruential generator (LCG) permutation, which maps indices via p(x) = (a * x + b) % N with gcd(a, N) = 1 for dataset length N. Because this linear permutation led to correlated data and phase shifts, Marin switched in Mantis (and going forward) to a Feistel-network pseudo-random permutation, which splits bit representations into halves and applies multiple mixing rounds with per-round keys.
